title: Simulation Helps Control, Manage Traffic
main_content:
Controlling traffic is a complex and high cost problem in many developed countries. It becomes more difficult and costly. But scientists and students at the Center for Advanced Transportation Technology, or CATT, at the University of Maryland are working to solve this problem. They are using simulation technologies to help government and private business control and react to changing traffic.

The online economics magazine Forbes.com says traffic congestion cost Americans $124 billion in 2014.

But scientists at the CATT laboratory are trying to reduce those costs. Michael Pack is CATT director.

The CATT Lab collects information from many sources, including roadside devices, GPS equipment and wireless phones.

About 60 students and 30 software developers observe traffic flow and manage the computer servers at all times. They also work to develop software and applications that can help traffic run smoother and safer.

The center shares its findings with firefighters, police, transportation departments and the military.

Mr. Pack says the goal is to help develop an intelligent system of road signals that will communicate with each other and with vehicles on the road.
